title: Canonical prompt matrix and API contract regression suite
creator: Mateo Ruiz
description: Build a canonical suite of prompts, contract tests, and CI jobs that validate API compatibility across streaming, tool/function calling, and structured-output code paths. The goal is a stable, reviewable nightly golden run plus per-PR contract checks that prevent silent regressions across SDK and server changes.
background: Recent rollout of the new streaming chunk framing and structured JSON validation layer revealed multiple subtle incompatibilities across SDK versions. We lack a centralized, reproducible set of "canonical" prompts that exercise edge cases for chunked streaming, partial tool call frames, nested JSON structured outputs, and compatibility shim fallbacks (legacy client behavior). Existing tests are scattered and only run in ad-hoc jobs.
goals: Ship a canonical prompt matrix covering core API modes (streaming text, streaming with tool/function calls, non-streaming function calls, structured JSON outputs, and legacy compatibility shims)
Implement contract tests that validate response framing, content-type semantics, function-call merging behavior, and JSON schema conformance
Add CI jobs: lightweight per-PR contract checks + nightly full golden-run that records diffs and surfaces regressions in Slack/email
Define a clear drift acceptance process for golden outputs with ML-similarity thresholds and required approvers
success_metrics: Reduce production compatibility incidents caused by API changes to zero for covered endpoints
Per-PR contract job pass rate >= 95% within first 2 months
Nightly golden-run alerts < 5 actionable diffs per week (after tuning)
acceptance_criteria: Canonical prompt matrix defined and committed under tests/canonical_prompts/*.yaml (covering >40 cases)
Contract test harness that runs against local runtime and hosted staging and returns machine-readable diffs
CI job 'contract-regressions/pr' runs in <10 minutes for a reduced subset and gates merge on failures
Nightly job 'contract-regressions/nightly' runs full matrix, uploads artifacts to s3://redwood-test-artifacts/contract-gold/ and posts summary to #ci-regressions with links
Documented golden drift process: sim-threshold, required reviewers, and change PR template in docs/golden-drift.md
tasks: Design canonical prompt taxonomy (streaming increments, tool call interleavings, malformed frames, structured JSON edge cases)
Author the initial 40+ prompts and expected canonical outputs (store both input and golden output files)
Implement contract runner that can replay prompts against runtime endpoints and SDK adapters (HTTP SSE, WebSocket, and polling)
Create lightweight per-PR subset and CI job configuration (GitHub Actions matrix + caching)
Add nightly job orchestration (Lambda/step function or GitHub scheduled) to run full matrix and snapshot artifacts
Wire Slack and email alerting with triage links and auto-assign rules
Add tooling to compute similarity metrics (token-level diff, normalized Levenshtein, embedding similarity) and output human-friendly diffs
Create PR and review checklist for golden updates (owner, ML-reviewer, API-product signoff)
Add tests for SDK compatibility shim: verify old client behavior preserved when compatibility flag is enabled
Run cross-team review with SDK, Console, and QA to validate coverage gaps
test_matrix_summary: Matrix axes: API version (v1, v1-beta), transport (SSE/http-streaming, websocket, polling), model families (redwood-llm-1, open-llm-compat), complexity (short/medium/long), tool-call patterns (single-call, chained-calls, partial-streamed-call), structured-output schemas (flat JSON, nested objects, arrays of objects), legacy client flags (compat-v1)
ci_integration_plan: Add two GitHub Actions workflows: 'contract-regressions/pr' (fast subset, runs on PRs and main pushes, 10m target) and 'contract-regressions/nightly' (full matrix, scheduled nightly). Use matrix strategy and self-hosted runners for GPU/CPU balance. Artifacts uploaded and retained for 30 days. Fail PR merge on contract-regressions/pr failure; nightly failures create a Slack incident thread for triage.
drift_acceptance_policy: If similarity score >= 0.95 (embedding cosine on normalized outputs) then auto-accept possible drift and open a 'golden-update' PR with diff and required reviewers. If 0.80 <= sim < 0.95, mark as 'manual review' and require at least 2 approvers. If sim < 0.80, block and create a regression incident with urgent paging. All updates must include: failing prompt, proposed golden replacement, root-cause analysis, and associated SDK/runtime PRs.
known_risks: Golden outputs for non-deterministic models may drift frequently; will require temperature seeding and deterministic model configs for canonical runs
Nightly full matrix may be expensive on hosted infra; need quota and caching of model downloads
Edge cases in streaming (partial JSON in chunks) are brittle and require robust reassembly logic in test runner
notes_from_review: PM review (Asha Patel): emphasize customer-impacted error modes and prioritize cases that trigger Console alerts
SDK lead (Ravi Kapoor): asked for explicit test hooks for both JS and Python SDKs; added requirement to validate client-side reassembly behavior
QA (Dana Morris): recommended synthetic fuzz cases for malformed frames to ensure robust parsing
timeline: Week 1: finalize prompt taxonomy and author 25 canonical prompts. Week 2: implement runner and PR CI subset. Week 3: create nightly orchestration and alerting. Week 4: cross-team validation and rollout. Contingency: extend by two weeks for drift tuning.
